places.title: Old Tbilisi – Kala (ძველი თბილისი)
places.why: The oldest quarter, on the right bank of the Mtkvari below Narikala: crooked lanes, brick houses with carved and glazed wooden balconies, courtyards shared by several families, and churches, a synagogue and a mosque a few streets apart. Most houses date from the 19th century, after the Persian sack of 1795.
places.note: The outline is the OSM neighbourhood of Kala (Kalaubani); Meidan Square and Shardeni Street lie inside it.

photos.file: Balcony of old house in Tbilisi.jpg
photos.author: Eka Samkharadze

places.title: Narikala Fortress (ნარიყალა)
places.why: The citadel on the ridge above the old town, first recorded in the 4th century and rebuilt by Arab emirs, Georgian kings and Persian governors; most of its walls date from the 16th–17th centuries. Its ruined walls and towers frame the widest view over Kala, the baths and the river; the ridge path continues to Kartlis Deda and the ruins of Shahtakhti.

places.title: Abanotubani – the sulphur baths (აბანოთუბანი)
places.why: The bath quarter at the foot of Narikala, built over the hot sulphur springs that gave Tbilisi its name: brick domes rising from a square at street level, and the blue-tiled Persian-style façade of the Orbeliani (Chreli) Bath. The Leghvtakhevi gorge behind it ends at a waterfall in the middle of the city.

places.title: Metekhi Church (მეტეხის ტაძარი)
places.why: A domed stone church on the cliff above the Mtkvari, facing the old town, rebuilt in the 1280s on the site of the royal residence. Next to it the equestrian statue of King Vakhtang Gorgasali, the founder of Tbilisi, looks across the river.

photos.file: Tbilisi The Metekhi Church of Assumption IMG 8842 1920.jpg
photos.author: Alexxx1979
U.S. Army photo by Sgt. LaShic Patterson

places.title: Holy Trinity Cathedral – Sameba (სამების საკათედრო ტაძარი)
places.why: The main cathedral of the Georgian Orthodox Church, built on Elia Hill after a competition: the traditional Georgian cross-domed church raised to the scale of a skyline landmark, its gilded cross seen from across the city, on a platform of terraces, gardens and smaller chapels.

photos.file: Architecture of Tbilisi, Part II - TbilisiArchitecture8024.jpg
photos.author: lumoplank

photos.file: Architecture of Tbilisi, Part II - TbilisiArchitecture8026.jpg
photos.author: lumoplank

places.title: Kartlis Deda – Mother of Georgia (ქართლის დედა)
places.why: The 20-metre figure on the Sololaki ridge, put up for the city’s 1500th anniversary: she holds a bowl of wine for guests and a sword for enemies. The path along the ridge from Narikala passes at her feet.

photos.file: Kartlis Deda - Mother of a Kartli or Mother of a Georgian - Photo by Mostafa Meraji 03.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

places.title: Bridge of Peace (მშვიდობის ხიდი)
places.architect: Michele De Lucchi; lighting by Philippe Martinaud
places.why: A footbridge of steel and glass over the Mtkvari between the old town and Rike Park, under a wavy glass canopy that lights up at night. Its contemporary form, set against the domes and balconies of Kala, made it a symbol of the city of the 2010s.

photos.file: Bridge of Peace on River Mtkvari.jpg
photos.author: Eka Samkharadze

places.title: Rike Park (რიყის პარკი)
places.area: Rike, left bank of the Mtkvari
places.why: The park on the left bank facing the old town, laid out in 2010 on a former riverside wasteland: lawns, fountains, a giant chessboard and the lower station of the cable car to Narikala, with the best view of Metekhi and the balconies of Kala across the water.
places.note: The tube-shaped concert hall by Studio Fuksas at the park’s edge is being demolished (permit of July 2026) and is not listed.

places.title: Mount Mtatsminda – park, funicular and TV tower (მთაწმინდა)
places.why: The holy mountain behind the city: a funicular of 1905 climbs past the church of St David to a park on the summit plateau with the widest view over Tbilisi, under the steel lattice of the 1972 television tower that marks the skyline at night.

photos.file: Mt Mtats'minda, Tbilisi, Georgia (view from Metekhi cliff).JPG
photos.author: Kober

photos.file: Tbilisi City - Urban Photos - Georgia Tourism 08.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

places.title: Rustaveli Avenue (რუსთაველის გამზირი)
places.why: Tbilisi’s main avenue, laid out in the 19th century from Freedom Square to Republic Square: in a kilometre and a half under plane trees it passes the Parliament, the National Museum and Gallery, Kashveti Church, the Opera and the Rustaveli Theatre.
places.note: The avenue was being rebuilt in 2025–26.

photos.file: 2024-05-02 Empty Rustaveli Avenue in Tbilisi during May 2024 protests.jpg
photos.author: Yuri Samoylov

places.title: Freedom Square (თავისუფლების მოედანი)
places.architect: Old City Hall: Paul Stern (remodelling); Freedom Monument: Zurab Tsereteli
places.year: City Hall remodelled after 1878, clock tower 1910; monument 2006
places.why: The square where the old town meets the 19th-century city, once Erivan Square: the Moorish-style former City Hall with its clock tower, Pushkin Garden on one side, and in the middle a column topped by a gilded St George slaying the dragon.

places.title: Sioni Cathedral (სიონის საკათედრო ტაძარი)
places.why: The old cathedral of Tbilisi in the middle of Kala, a cross-domed church of yellow tuff rebuilt many times after invasions since the 7th century, with a free-standing bell tower of 1425 and a Russian-built one of 1812 beside it.

photos.file: Tbilisi Sioni Cathedral in Georgia, Spring 2011.jpg
photos.author: savl_ukr from Kyiv, Ukraine

places.title: Anchiskhati Basilica (ანჩისხატი)
places.why: The oldest surviving church in Tbilisi, a three-nave basilica of the 6th century hidden among old-town houses, with a brick bell tower of 1675. Its name comes from the icon of Ancha, brought here in the 17th century.

places.title: Gabriadze Theatre Clock Tower (გაბრიაძის საათის კოშკი)
places.why: A crooked, leaning tower put together by the puppeteer and artist Rezo Gabriadze beside his marionette theatre from old bricks, tiles and hand-painted panels; an angel strikes the bell on the hour.

photos.file: Detail of Shavteli street clock, Tbilisi (14831993928).jpg
photos.author: Gill M L

photos.file: Rezo Gabriadze Marionette Theater Clock Tower (8).jpg
photos.author: Benreis

places.title: Dry Bridge and Dedaena Park (მშრალი ხიდი)
places.why: A brick arch of 1851 left dry when its arm of the Mtkvari was drained in 1933, and the riverside park beside it: together the site of the city’s open-air flea and art market, with Soviet badges, cameras, silverware and paintings laid out along the parapets.

photos.file: 2025-03-30 Old cameras at the Dry Bridge Market, Tbilisi 2.jpg
photos.author: Alexkom000

places.title: National Botanical Garden of Georgia (ეროვნული ბოტანიკური ბაღი)
places.why: Old royal gardens in the gorge behind Narikala, turned into a botanical garden in 1845: paths along the Tsavkisistskali stream, a waterfall, a bridge across the ravine and wild hillsides a few minutes from the baths.

photos.file: National Botanical Garden of Georgia باغ های بوتانیکال در شهر تفلیس گرجستان 11.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

photos.file: Autumn season in Butanic Garden فصل پاییز در باغ بوتانیکال تفلیس 08.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

photos.file: Autumn season in Butanic Garden فصل پاییز در باغ بوتانیکال تفلیس 12.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

places.title: Sololaki (სოლოლაკი)
places.why: The district under the Sololaki ridge where merchants and nobility built their town houses in the 19th and early 20th centuries: eclectic and Art Nouveau façades, iron balconies and entrance halls with painted walls, tiled floors and sweeping stairs.

photos.file: A street in Sololaki. Tbilisi (Photo A. Muhranoff, 2011).jpg
photos.author: Aleksey Muhranoff

places.title: Chronicle of Georgia (საქართველოს მატიანე)
places.why: Sixteen bronze-clad pillars about 30 metres tall on a hill above the Tbilisi Sea, cast with scenes of Georgian kings, saints and battles above a band of the life of Christ: a vast, unfinished monument reached by a long stair.

photos.file: Georgiaren Kronikak (Tbilisi) - The Chronicle of Georgia - Tagzania - 1775459624045.jpg
photos.author: MSO (Tagzania user ID: 3984)

photos.file: Georgiaren Kronikak (Tbilisi) - The Chronicle of Georgia - Tagzania - 1775459623095.jpg
photos.author: MSO (Tagzania user ID: 3984)

photos.file: Georgiaren Kronikak (Tbilisi) - The Chronicle of Georgia - Tagzania - 1775459623710.jpg
photos.author: MSO (Tagzania user ID: 3984)

places.title: Bank of Georgia HQ – former Ministry of Highways (საქართველოს ბანკის სათავო ოფისი)
places.why: Five layers of two-storey blocks stacked crosswise on a few concrete cores, 18 storeys up a slope above the Mtkvari: Chakhava’s Space City idea of a building that leaves the ground free. Chakhava was the minister of highways and his own client.

photos.file: Architecture of Tbilisi, Part II - TbilisiArchitecture8017.jpg
photos.author: lumoplank

places.title: Palace of Rituals – Wedding Palace (რიტუალების სასახლე)
places.why: A late-Soviet temple for civil weddings on a hill above the river: rounded volumes like the apses of an Orthodox church, and a hall roofed by a stepped wooden vault taken from the traditional east Georgian darbazi house.

places.title: Former Tbilisi Archaeological Museum (ყოფილი თბილისის არქეოლოგიური მუზეუმი)
places.architect: Shota Kavlashvili and Shota Gvantseladze; relief by Tengiz Kikalishvili
places.why: Three tuff-clad cylinders in a row on a hill above an ancient burial ground, partly built over old water reservoirs; the long relief at the entrance shows a figure lying in a grave.
places.note: Closed and abandoned; only the exterior can be seen.

places.title: Nutsubidze Skybridge – Shatili Housing Complex (საცხოვრებელი კომპლექსი „შატილი“)
places.why: Three panel-built housing blocks stepped up a steep slope and joined by concrete bridges high above the ground: residents of the upper blocks reach the street through the lifts of the lower one.

photos.file: Houses with bridges on the Nutsubidze Slope.jpg
photos.author: Nermosh

places.title: Former Scientific-Technical Library (სამეცნიერო-ტექნიკური ბიბლიოთეკა)
places.why: A long library block wrapped in rows of sail-shaped concrete sunshades, with rounded portals at both ends; one floor still keeps its reliefs and tapestry.
places.note: Mostly closed and on the endangered list of SOS Brutalism.

photos.file: Former Building of the Science-Technology Department of the National Scientific Library of Georgia, Tbilisi.jpg
photos.author: FingerWiki

places.title: Expo Georgia – former Exhibition of Economic Achievements (ექსპოჯორჯია)
places.architect: Main pavilion: Levan Mamaladze and others; mosaic by Leonardo Shengelia
places.why: The Soviet exhibition park of Georgia: eleven pavilions with parabolic roofs and glass walls in a park of fountains, sculptures and reliefs, with a full-wall mosaic of cosmonauts and scientists of 1963.

photos.file: Didube, Tbilisi, Georgia — Bas-relief in Expo Georgia Gallery.jpg
photos.author: Giorgi Balakhadze

places.title: Former Auditorium of the Industrial-Pedagogical College (აუდიტორია)
places.why: A sculptural concrete hall attached to a college block, with echoes of Constructivism and Latin American modernism; until 2018 its façade carried a winged figure by Zurab Tsereteli.
places.note: Out of use and lived in by displaced families; seen from outside.

places.title: Laguna Vere – former Central Water Sports Complex (ლაგუნა ვერე)
places.architect: Shota Kavlashvili, Ramaz Kiknadze and Guram Abuladze; mosaic by Nikolai Ignatov
places.why: The great Soviet swimming complex at the mouth of the Vere: three pools with brutalist diving towers, stands for 5,500, and an embankment façade of yellow tuff with a mosaic along its whole length.
places.note: Closed since 2013; in 2026 a new owner announced its restoration.

places.title: Public Service Hall (იუსტიციის სახლი)
places.area: Old Tbilisi, riverside by Europe Square
places.why: Eleven white petal-shaped canopies of steel lattice and fibreglass on tree-like columns, up to 35 metres high, shelter a public hall and office blocks for the state’s citizen services: a landmark of the reform years on the riverside.

photos.file: Tbilisi Public Service Hall Building IMG 8999 1920.jpg
photos.author: Alexxx1979

photos.file: Interior of the House of Justice in Tbilisi, Georgia.jpg
photos.author: FingerWiki

places.title: Chess Palace and Alpine Club (ჭადრაკის სასახლე)
places.why: A three-storey building stepped into the slope of Vere Park around a hall rising through all floors, ringed by galleries and closed by movable panels of wood intarsia; stone and crown-shaped blocks clad its walls.
places.note: Under reconstruction until the end of 2027.

photos.file: 2024-07-20 Entrance to Nona Gaprindashvili Chess Palace.jpg
photos.author: Yuri Samoylov

places.title: Tbilisi Concert Hall – Philharmonic (საკონცერტო დარბაზი)
places.architect: Ivane Chkhenkeli; Muse by Merab Berdzenishvili
places.why: A concert hall for over 2,000 listeners whose circular foyer opens to the streets around it; in front of it stands Merab Berdzenishvili’s bronze Muse.

places.title: Mukhatgverdi Ceremonial Hall (მუხათგვერდის რიტუალების დარბაზი)
places.why: A twin-towered farewell hall on a hill above the cemetery, part of an ensemble of four buildings by Djorbenadze that fuse Georgian church forms with the sculptural concrete of Tange and Le Corbusier.

places.title: Meama Coffee Production Plant (მეამას ყავის ქარხანა)
places.why: An L-shaped factory wrapped in folded walls of poured concrete under an undulating roof of wild grass that rises and falls with the machines inside; grand prize of the ArchDaily & Strelka Award 2019.

places.title: Tbilisi Circus (თბილისის ცირკი)
places.architect: Nikolay Neprintsev, Vladimer Urushadze and Stepan Satunts
places.why: A neoclassical rotunda for 2,000 spectators on a hill above Heroes Square, the circus of the Stalin years, restored and reopened in 2011.

places.title: Stamba and Rooms Hotel – former printing house (სტამბა)
places.why: The 1930s printing works of the Soviet newspapers turned into hotels, cafés and a cultural centre: a five-storey atrium planted with trees on an old drying beam, under a pool with a glass bottom.

places.title: Fabrika (ფაბრიკა)
places.why: An abandoned Soviet sewing factory reopened in 2016 as a hostel, studios and a public courtyard of small bars and shops, keeping the zodiac relief over its entrance and walls painted by street artists.

photos.file: Fabrika Tbilisi, an urban culture hub in the capital of Georgia.jpg
photos.author: Alf Altendorf

places.title: Georgian National Museum (საქართველოს ეროვნული მუზეუმი)
places.architect: Nikolay Severov; also attributed to M. Neprintsev
places.why: The building of the old Caucasian Museum on Rustaveli Avenue, dressed in medieval Georgian ornament: the country’s main museum, with the Dmanisi hominid fossils and the pre-Christian gold of its Archaeological Treasury.

photos.file: Museum of the Soviet Occupation in Tbilisi.jpg
photos.author: Jeremy Teigen from USA

photos.file: Georgian National Museum موزه ملی تفلیس- گرجستان 02.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

photos.file: Საქართველოს ეროვნული მუზეუმი موزه ملی گرجستان در شهر تفلیس 34.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

places.title: National Gallery – Blue Gallery (ეროვნული გალერეა)
places.why: Built in 1888 as the Temple of Glory, a museum of the Caucasian wars modelled on the Palazzo delle Esposizioni in Rome; known as the Blue Gallery after its colour, it now shows Georgian painting, with a hall of works by Niko Pirosmani.

places.title: Gudiashvili Square (გუდიაშვილის მოედანი)
places.why: A small old square already drawn on the city plan of 1735, whose houses with wooden balconies and carved details were restored one by one in 2015–2021 after decades of decay.

photos.file: Blue House on corner Guliashvili Square.jpg
photos.author: Jelger Groeneveld

photos.file: 2023-12-16 Traditional house in Tbilisi at Gudiashvili Square.jpg
photos.author: Alexkom000

places.title: Tbilisi Opera and Ballet Theatre (ოპერისა და ბალეტის თეატრი)
places.why: The neo-Moorish opera house of 1896, built after the first theatre burnt down in 1874: horseshoe arches, slender columns and patterned façades on Rustaveli Avenue, with a gilded auditorium restored in 2016.

photos.file: Tbilisi Opera House - Main Hall from Stage.jpg
photos.author: Hundnase

places.title: Betlemi Quarter (ბეთლემი)
places.year: Upper Betlemi church 1727; Lower Betlemi rebuilt 1868–1870
places.why: A hillside quarter of stepped lanes and stairs between Sololaki and Narikala, around the Upper Betlemi church of 1727, with its upper courses of black stone, and the Lower Betlemi church; many of its houses were restored in a long programme of ICOMOS Georgia.

photos.file: Holy Mother of God Church of Bethlehem, Tbilisi.jpg
photos.author: Ian.Climacus

photos.file: Armenian church Saint Bethlehem in Tbilisi (lower monument group) 15.jpg
photos.author: Soghomon Matevosyan

photos.file: Armenian church Saint Bethlehem in Tbilisi (lower monument group) 03.jpg
photos.author: Soghomon Matevosyan

photos.file: Armenian church Saint Bethlehem in Tbilisi (lower monument group) 05.jpg
photos.author: Soghomon Matevosyan

places.title: Mtatsminda Pantheon and St David’s Church (მთაწმინდის პანთეონი)
places.why: The churchyard of St David’s church halfway up Mtatsminda, a pantheon since 1929: Griboyedov and Nino Chavchavadze, Ilia Chavchavadze, Vazha-Pshavela and Galaktion Tabidze lie on terraces above the city, on the way up by funicular or on foot.

places.title: Kalantarov House (კალანტაროვის სახლი)
places.why: A neo-Moorish mansion of 1908 whose entrance hall has turquoise and orange walls, lancet arches and a stalactite ceiling, repeated all the way up the stair to a round stained-glass skylight.

places.title: Parliament Building (პარლამენტის შენობა)
places.why: Built as the Soviet Georgian House of Government on the site of a demolished cathedral: two buildings joined by a courtyard of stairs and fountains, with a monumental arcade on Rustaveli Avenue that mixes neoclassicism with Georgian motifs.

places.title: Jumah Mosque (ჯუმა მეჩეთი)
places.why: The only surviving mosque of old Tbilisi, a red-brick building of 1895 with arched windows and an octagonal minaret above the bath domes, where Sunni and Shia Muslims pray side by side.

photos.file: Juma Mosque of Tbilisi from the top.jpg
photos.author: Reda Kerbush

places.title: Mtskheta: Jvari Monastery and Svetitskhoveli Cathedral (მცხეთა)
places.why: The ancient capital at the meeting of the Aragvi and the Mtkvari, 20 km from Tbilisi and a UNESCO site: the hilltop Jvari monastery of about 600, the model for a whole family of Georgian domed churches, and the cathedral of Svetitskhoveli inside its 18th-century walls.

places.title: The Telegraph – former Central Post and Telegraph (ტელეგრაფი)
places.architect: Vladimir Aleksi-Meskhishvili and Teimuraz Mikashavidze; conversion by Neri&Hu
places.why: The brutalist post and telegraph office of 1980, clad in Bolnisi tuff, long abandoned and converted into a hotel by Neri&Hu, who kept its raw concrete and opened the ground floor as public passages around a courtyard.

places.title: Aghmashenebeli Avenue (აღმაშენებლის გამზირი)
places.why: The main street of the 19th-century left bank, lined with classical and Art Nouveau façades; about seventy buildings were restored from 2010, and the lower part from Saarbrücken Square is a pedestrian street.

places.title: Seilanov Brothers House (სეილანოვების სახლი)
places.why: The house of two tobacco merchants, whose entrance hall has a carpet-like mosaic floor with their name and the date 1911, and painted panels of the continents around a semicircular stair lit by a glass ceiling.

places.title: Tbilisi History Museum – Karvasla (ქარვასლა)
places.why: A caravanserai by Sioni Cathedral built by King Rostom in the 17th century, rebuilt by a merchant after 1821 and given a new street front in 1908–1912: three centuries of layers that now house the city’s history museum.

photos.author: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

places.title: Queen Darejan’s Palace – Sachino (დარეჯანის სასახლე)
places.why: The palace King Erekle II built for Queen Darejan on the Avlabari cliff: a compact stone building whose corner tower is wrapped in a round, carved wooden balcony looking over Metekhi and Narikala.

photos.file: Queen Darejan Palace in Tbilisi, Georgia.jpg
photos.author: Andrew Milligan sumo

photos.file: Queen Darejan Palace, Tbilisi (Photo A. Muhranoff, 2011).jpg
photos.author: Aleksey Muhranoff

photos.file: Old Tbilisi. Palace of Queen Darejan.jpg
photos.author: Ekkatterrinna

photos.file: "საჩინო" - დარეჯან დედოფლის სასახლე - ხედი ფერისცვალების ეკლესიის ეზოდან.jpg
photos.author: Ekkatterrinna

places.title: Rustaveli Theatre (რუსთაველის თეატრი)
places.why: Built for the city’s Artists’ Society, with late-Baroque and Rococo ornament on the façade and in the auditorium. Its basement hall was painted in 1919 by Lado Gudiashvili, David Kakabadze, Sergey Sudeikin and the Toidze brothers, the meeting place of Tbilisi’s avant-garde.

photos.file: Rustaveli National Theater in Georgia (Europe), built 19th century in Rococo style.jpg
photos.author: DDohler

photos.file: Relief ornament at the Rustaveli Theatre, Tbilisi, Georgia.jpg
photos.author: dkowi

places.title: Kashveti Church of St George (ქაშვეთის ეკლესია)
places.why: A stone church on Rustaveli Avenue, opposite the Parliament, modelled on the 11th-century cathedral of Samtavisi: carved stone crosses and window frames in the medieval Georgian manner, and inside murals painted by Lado Gudiashvili in 1947.

places.title: Writers’ House of Georgia (მწერალთა სახლი)
places.why: The mansion of the brandy maker David Sarajishvili, Art Nouveau mixed with neo-Baroque, with a terrace of Villeroy & Boch tiles and a garden. Given to the writers’ union after 1921, it was the meeting place of the Blue Horns poets and now holds a museum of repressed writers.

photos.author: Raymond Zoller from unterwegs. on the road

places.title: Zurab Tsereteli Museum of Modern Art (თანამედროვე ხელოვნების მუზეუმი)
places.architect: Conversion of the former Cadet Corps building
places.why: The 19th-century Cadet Corps building on Rustaveli Avenue, its façade kept and its interior rebuilt as a museum in 2012 for the work of the sculptor Zurab Tsereteli and temporary shows of contemporary art.

photos.file: Zurab Tsereteli Museum Of Modern Art 1.jpg
photos.author: Gobrona

photos.file: Zurab Tsereteli Museum Of Modern Art.jpg
photos.author: Gobrona

photos.file: Zurab Tsereteli Museum Of Modern Art 3.jpg
photos.author: Gobrona

places.title: Art Museum of Georgia – Shalva Amiranashvili (ხელოვნების მუზეუმი)
places.why: The country’s main collection of medieval Georgian art, its goldsmith work and enamels, housed since 1950 in the neoclassical building of 1838 that was the Tiflis Theological Seminary.

photos.file: Royal Persian Paintings - Georgian Art Museum - Tbilisi.jpg
photos.author: PersianDutchNetwork

places.title: Georgian Museum of Fine Arts (ქართული სახვითი ხელოვნების მუზეუმი)
places.why: A private museum built from scratch for Georgian painting: four volumes of Bolnisi tuff stepping down the slope towards Gudiashvili Street, with 31 halls on three floors joined by glass stairs.

photos.file: Georgian Museum of Fine Arts Facade.jpg
photos.author: Mnj070

photos.file: Georgian Museum of Fine Arts Glass Staircase.jpg
photos.author: Mnj070

places.title: Ceremonial Palace of Georgia (სახელმწიფო ცერემონიების სასახლე)
places.architect: Attributed to Michele De Lucchi and Giga Batiashvili (disputed); dome: Vakhtang Zesashvili and Franco Zagari
places.why: The former presidential palace on the Avlabari ridge, built over a 19th-century gendarmerie: a colonnaded body under a glass dome that dominates the left bank next to Sameba and Metekhi.

photos.file: Rike and the Presidential Palace in Tbilisi 2010.jpg
photos.author: Kober

places.title: IMELI – former Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute (იმელი)
places.architect: Alexey Shchusev; reliefs by Iakob Nikoladze and Tamar Abakelia
places.why: Shchusev’s institute of 1938, Socialist Classicism with Constructivist massing and Georgian motifs, where the 1995 constitution was adopted. Only its colonnaded façade survives, in front of the Biltmore Hotel and its 138-metre glass tower.

places.title: Art Palace – Oldenburg Palace (ხელოვნების სასახლე)
places.why: A palace built by Prince Constantine of Oldenburg for his wife Agrippina Japaridze, mixing Gothic and Islamic motifs. Restored in 2011, it houses the museum of Georgian theatre, music and film.

photos.file: Love Tower, Art Palace, Tbilisi, Georgia.jpg
photos.author: Giorgi1975 at Georgian Wikipedia

photos.file: Main entrance, Art Palace, Tbilisi, Georgia.jpg
photos.author: Giorgi1975 at Georgian Wikipedia

places.title: Former House of Political Education – Mosaic Business Centre (ბიზნეს ცენტრი მოზაიკა)
places.architect: V. Abramashvili, G. Mirianashvili, S. Melashvili, G. Salukvadze; mosaic by Zurab Tsereteli
places.why: A late-Soviet block on Aghmashenebeli Avenue whose façade carries one of Zurab Tsereteli’s largest abstract mosaics, chosen instead of a planned scene of Lenin and workers. Today a business centre named after the mosaic.

places.title: Former Hotel London (სასტუმრო „ლონდონი“)
places.why: A hotel of the 1870s by Otto Simonson, now flats, whose entrance hall keeps its marble stair and painted walls, the central composition by an Italian artist.

places.title: Radisson Blu Iveria Hotel (ივერია)
places.architect: Otar Kalandarishvili with I. Tskhomelidze; rebuilt by GRAFT
places.why: The 18-storey modernist hotel of 1967, for years the tallest building in the city and from 1992 to 2004 home to refugees from Abkhazia. It was stripped to its steel frame and rebuilt by the Berlin firm GRAFT with a new glass façade.

places.title: Tbilisi Prosecutor’s Office (ქალაქ თბილისის პროკურატურა)
places.why: Glass volumes stacked and shifted inside a black frame, with a passage carved through the ground floor and terraces on the staggered floors: one of the transparent public buildings of the Saakashvili years.

places.title: Mediatheque, Veterans Park (მედიათეკა)
places.why: A municipal library for a housing district: a fabric-clad steel outline cantilevered 12 metres over the entrance, glass rooms inside, oval rooms carrying the upper floor and a round blue courtyard, reached by a ramp shaped like a children’s slide.

places.title: Former Third Girls’ Gymnasium – ‘Tbilisi Hogwarts’ (მესამე ქალთა გიმნაზია)
places.why: A Gothic Revival school at the top of Sololaki, with tall pointed windows of small coloured panes and wooden balconies; still a school, nicknamed the city’s Hogwarts.

photos.file: თბილისის მეექვსე საავტორო სკოლა, ყოფილი კეთილშობილ ქალთა გერმანული პანსიონი.jpg
photos.author: Lasha ge

photos.file: 3-я женская гимназия (2), ул. Ладо Асатиани 28, арх. Озеров Александр Григорьевич.jpg
photos.author: Pavel Umovskiy

places.title: Avlabari (ავლაბარი)
places.why: The old quarter on the left bank, long the centre of Armenian Tbilisi: wooden balconies and inner courtyards on the slope between Metekhi and Sameba, with Armenian churches and the Armenian Pantheon among its streets.

places.title: Tbilisi State Academy of Arts (სამხატვრო აკადემია)
places.architect: G. Ivanov; rebuilt by Simon Kldiashvili; restored by Nodar Amashukeli’s team
places.why: The mansion of Vardan Arshakuni, whose European façade hides halls decorated by Qajar artists from Iran: mirror mosaics, stucco medallions and stalactite friezes, restored around 2020.

places.title: Great Synagogue (თბილისის დიდი სინაგოგა)
places.why: The largest synagogue in Georgia, built by Jews from Akhaltsikhe: a red-brick building in Moorish and Romanesque revival forms, set into the slope so that its back opens on the street above.

places.title: Open Air Museum of Ethnography (ეთნოგრაფიული მუზეუმი ღია ცის ქვეშ)
places.why: About 70 houses, towers, wineries and mills moved from every region of Georgia onto a wooded hillside: east Georgian darbazi with their stepped wooden domes, wooden houses of the west, Svan and Khevsur towers.

photos.file: Ethnographic Museum of Tbilisi. The ethnographers house. 2.jpg
photos.author: Kakhi Kuloshvili

photos.file: Ethnographic Museum of Tbilisi. House of kakhetian. 2.jpg
photos.author: Kakhi Kuloshvili

photos.file: Ethnographic Museum of Tbilisi. House of kakhetian. 1.jpg
photos.author: Kakhi Kuloshvili

places.title: Tbilisi State University, First Building (თსუ პირველი კორპუსი)
places.why: Built as the gymnasium of the Georgian nobility by the first academically trained Georgian architect: a Renaissance-style front with a domed central bay and giant Corinthian pilasters, raised on a wide stair and ramps. The university has used it since 1918.

photos.file: Tbilisi, Georgia — Tbilisi State University, I Corpus's front view.jpg
photos.author: Giorgi Balakhadze

places.title: Kikodze Street 9 – the ‘Italian villa’ (კიკოძის 9)
places.why: An Art Nouveau house with a stone balcony over a front garden and a monogram on its façade, and a wrought-iron stair in its entrance hall.

places.title: Tbilisi Central Station (თბილისის ცენტრალური სადგური)
places.architect: R. Bairamashvili, I. Kavlashvili, G. Shavdia, A. Jibladze; conversion by Zwarts & Jansma
places.why: A late-Soviet station built as a bridge across the tracks, joining two parts of the city in one concrete structure; since 2010 it is also a shopping centre.

places.title: Melik-Azaryants House (მელიქ-აზარიანცის სახლი)
places.why: A vast Art Nouveau apartment house, a city block for the merchant Alexander Melik-Azaryants with shops, a cinema and its own power plant; an asymmetric façade of contrasting textures and reliefs, and a painted entrance hall.

places.title: Ter-Akopova House (ტერ-აკოპოვას სახლი)
places.why: A Renaissance-revival house whose entrance hall has a mosaic floor spelling the owner’s name, Evelina Ter-Akopova, in black marble letters, under painted walls and a stair.

places.title: Boris Paichadze Dinamo Arena (დინამო არენა)
places.architect: Archil Kurdiani and Gia Kurdiani; engineer Shalva Gazashvili
places.why: Georgia’s largest stadium: the upper tier of 1976 rests on cantilevers carried by 58 pylons, under a 30-metre cantilevered roof. The former pool beneath the stands is now the Bassiani club.

photos.file: Boris Paichadze Dinamo Arena, Samtredia - Qarabağ 1.jpg
photos.author: Emin Allahverdi

photos.file: Boris Paichadze Dinamo Arena, Samtredia - Qarabağ.jpg
photos.author: Emin Allahverdi

places.title: Baratashvili Bridge (ბარათაშვილის ხიდი)
places.why: A road and foot bridge over the Mtkvari of 1966, on the site of the older Mukhrani Bridge, whose railings carry bronze figures of couples, with views of Metekhi and the old town.

places.title: Ateshgah – Zoroastrian fire temple (ათეშგა)
places.why: A cubic brick fire temple hidden in a courtyard of the Betlemi quarter, said to be the northernmost of the Zoroastrian world and later used as a mosque; now protected under a light curved roof.

photos.file: Ateshgah - Persian Fire Temple in Tbilisi.jpg
photos.author: PersianDutchNetwork

places.title: Chavchanidze House (ჩავჩანიძის სახლი)
places.why: The house of the merchant Erasti Chavchanidze, whose stairwell was painted by Italian artists with scenes from Rustaveli’s Knight in the Panther’s Skin, after Mihály Zichy’s illustrations.

photos.file: Дом купца Эраста Чавчанизе на пр. Агмашенебели, г. Тбилиси (1903 г.).jpg
photos.author: Георгий Анзорович Давиташвили

photos.file: 2025-03-26 Main entrance of the house of Erast Chavchanidze.jpg
photos.author: Yuri Samoylov

places.title: Kaleidoscope House (ბეთლემის 3)
places.why: A two-storey old-town house whose wooden balcony and stair are glazed with coloured glass in large, irregular fragments, a free take on the Persian-style glazed windows of Tbilisi.

places.title: Armenian Cathedral of St George (სურბ გევორქი)
places.why: The cathedral of Tbilisi’s Armenians, a brick church of the 13th century with murals by Hovnatan Hovnatanian and Gevorg Bashinjaghian; the poet Sayat-Nova is buried at its door.

photos.file: Armenian church Saint Gevorg in Tbilisi. 05.jpg
photos.author: Soghomon Matevosyan

photos.file: Saint Gevorg Armenian Church, Old Tbilisi - Սուրբ Գևորգ հայկական եկեղեցի, Հին Թբիլիսի.jpg
photos.author: GeoO

photos.file: Armenian church Saint Gevorg in Tbilisi. 14.jpg
photos.author: Soghomon Matevosyan

photos.file: Armenian church Saint Gevorg in Tbilisi. 19.jpg
photos.author: Soghomon Matevosyan

places.title: Arashenda Building (არაშენდა)
places.why: A late-Soviet hotel begun in 1982 and never finished, its concrete shell later taken over as flats: a strange landmark near the Chronicle of Georgia.

photos.file: Arashenda Building in Tbilisi, view from the Chronicle of Georgia.jpg
photos.author: FingerWiki

places.title: Ortachala Central Bus Station (ორთაჭალის ავტოსადგური)
places.architect: Shota Kavlashvili, Ramaz Kiknadze, Vladimer Kurtishvili; mosaic by Zurab Tsereteli
places.why: A bus station on a riverside slope, ringed by roadways with a bridge and ramps up to a glazed central hall; its stone façade carries Zurab Tsereteli’s mosaic of the history of transport.

places.title: Wine Factory N1 (ღვინის ქარხანა N1)
places.why: David Sarajishvili’s winery of the 1890s, brick with white stone arches, whose cellars of pointed brick vaults now hold restaurants and bars, keeping its Soviet mosaics and metal doors.

places.title: Georgian National Academy of Sciences (მეცნიერებათა აკადემია)
places.why: A post-war Stalinist building with a tower and Georgian ornament, closing the upper end of Rustaveli Avenue; in its courtyard stands the lower station of the cable car to Mtatsminda.

photos.file: Academy of Sciences of Georgia, Tbilisi.JPG
photos.author: Kober

photos.file: 2024-05-04 View of Tbilisi from Mikhail Tverskoy church.jpg
photos.author: Alexkom000

places.title: Bozarjants House (ბოზარჯიანცის სახლი)
places.why: The Art Nouveau house of a tobacco merchant whose façade won the city’s prize for the best façade in 1915; a film set for several Soviet classics.

places.title: Anna Madatova House (მადათოვას სახლი)
places.why: A house hidden from the street, reached through a deep tunnel and a ceremonial stair, with painted walls at the entrance and a domed arbour on its terrace.

places.title: National Library of Georgia (ეროვნული ბიბლიოთეკა)
places.why: Built as the Bank of the Nobility and an early revival of medieval Georgian architecture: a deep loggia on massive piers, a corner tower, carved window frames and a painted vaulted banking hall that is now the reading room.

photos.file: Wikiwyprawa 2015 Budynek Narodowej Biblioteki Parlamentu Gruzińskiego, proj Anatolij Kalgin i Henryk Hryniewski 5.jpg
photos.author: slawkuwal

photos.file: National Parliamentary Library of Georgia, Building №1.jpg
photos.author: Alsandro

photos.file: Wikiwyprawa 2015 Budynek Narodowej Biblioteki Parlamentu Gruzińskiego, proj Anatolij Kalgin i Henryk Hryniewski 12.jpg
photos.author: slawkuwal

photos.file: Wikiwyprawa 2015 Budynek Narodowej Biblioteki Parlamentu Gruzińskiego, proj Anatolij Kalgin i Henryk Hryniewski 3.jpg
photos.author: slawkuwal

places.title: Tbilisi State Conservatoire (კონსერვატორია)
places.why: An eclectic music school with a column portal turned towards Rustaveli Avenue and Art Nouveau interiors; its small hall of 1904 keeps the original decoration.

places.title: Kldisubani Church of St George (კლდისუბნის ეკლესია)
places.why: A small single-nave church of 1753 under the rock of Narikala, built by an Armenian merchant, used as a workshop in Soviet times and reconsecrated in 1991.

photos.author: Aleksey Muhranoff

photos.file: Kldisubani St. George's Church in Tbilisi.jpg
photos.author: Saskia Heijltjes

places.title: Norashen Church (ნორაშენი)
places.why: An Armenian brick church of the Holy Mother of God with classical pediments on its façades and 18th-century frescoes by Hovnatan Hovnatanian, standing next to Jvaris Mama.
places.note: Closed and disputed between the Armenian and Georgian churches.

photos.file: Norashen Holy Mother of God Armenian Church 0008.jpg
photos.author: dashis

places.title: Jvaris Mama Church (ჯვარის მამა)
places.why: A small domed brick church of the old town whose dome rests on the walls rather than on piers; it belonged to the Georgian Monastery of the Cross in Jerusalem, which gave it its name.

places.title: Marjanishvili Theatre (მარჯანიშვილის თეატრი)
places.why: An Art Nouveau People’s House built by the Zubalashvili brothers for the public of Chugureti, home since 1930 of the theatre founded by Kote Marjanishvili.

places.title: Agrohub Riverbank (აგროჰაბი)
places.why: A market hall, restaurant and car park stacked in raw concrete on the right bank of the Mtkvari, with a restaurant terrace on top.

places.title: Vake Park (ვაკის პარკი)
places.why: The great post-war park on the slope of the Trialeti ridge: a monumental stair and cascade of fountains climb from Chavchavadze Avenue to the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and a Victory figure, with shady red-sand paths on both sides.

photos.file: Gardens and parks in Tbilisi پارک ها و مبلمان شهری در تفلیس 12.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

places.title: Mziuri Park (მზიური)
places.why: A children’s park of 1982 in the gorge of the Vere, rebuilt after the 2015 flood with a concrete skatepark and parkour ground that follows the old riverbed under the bridge.

places.title: Turtle Lake (კუს ტბა)
places.why: A small lake on the wooded slope above Vake, reached by cable car from Chavchavadze Avenue, with paths on to the Open Air Museum of Ethnography and Mtatsminda.

photos.file: Turtle Lake in Tbilisi, autumn season.jpg
photos.author: Mostafameraji

places.title: Lisi Lake (ლისის ტბა)
places.why: A lake in the dry steppe hills north-west of the city, with a path around the shore and open views over the hills; a favourite of locals for a walk or a run.

places.title: Tbilisi Urban Forest (ურბანული ტყე)
places.why: The replanting of the cliffside below Narikala, where ageing Soviet pine plantations were dying: drifts of shrubland, hackberry forest and fruit trees, chosen by slope and soil, with new trails from the Betlemi stairs to the Botanical Garden.

places.title: 9 April Park (9 აპრილის ბაღი)
places.why: The city’s first public park, the former Alexander Garden, on two terraces between Rustaveli Avenue and the river, behind Kashveti Church and the National Gallery; renamed for the victims of 9 April 1989.

other.note: National Gallery, on the edge of the park

places.title: Mushtaid Garden (მუშთაიდის ბაღი)
places.why: An old garden on the left bank with an alley of relict zelkova trees and one of the world’s first children’s railways (1935); the silkworm station of 1892 at its edge is now the State Silk Museum.

places.title: Vere Park (ვერის ბაღი)
places.why: A neighbourhood park of 1934 laid out on the old Vere cemetery, with a formal French-style entrance and flower parterres; the Soviet-modernist Chess Palace stands inside it.
